output.summary: KEP-2258 proposes a kubelet API and kubectl support so cluster administrators can stream node logs (systemd/journald services, /var/log files, and Windows event/log files) without SSH access to the node. The KEP is recorded as implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: Troubleshooting control-plane and worker nodes required administrators to SSH into nodes to read services' logs such as kube-proxy or kubelet. The KEP restricts access to cluster administrators because node logs are sensitive. Reviewers accepted the design after debate over whether to hide the journald-versus-file distinction, and the agreed direction was a heuristic lookup by service name.

alternatives.option: Client-side log reader deployed on the nodes to redirect logs
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this would need privileged container support on Windows and would not help when containers fail to launch on the node.

alternatives.option: Require callers to specify journal versus file explicitly for each query
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (thockin) objected that users should not have to know the difference; the thread moved toward a heuristic that looks up the service name in the journal and then /var/log.

alternatives.option: Ship logs off-node to a central store
alternatives.why_not: Raised by thockin as a comparison point; the sources do not record a specific rejection rationale beyond the need for the added complexity to be justified.

evidence.quote: A simpler and more elegant method would be to allow them to use a kubelet API or kubectl plugin to also view these logs similar to using it for other interactions with the cluster.
I have updated the KEP to reflect the heuristic approach you suggested. Please take a look.
Confined to admins this feature should be roughly proportionally as expensive as any other admin command, and an admin has other ways to attack the node.
My fear is that if we implement with a lot of control we will have a hard time removing them, whereas if we start with relatively little control, we may not need them at all.
If the authorization is limited the same way as current node log access, and kubelet admins have the ability to disable logs by setting enableSystemLogHandler: false, this lgtm for sig-auth
